 The military’s quiet rebellion against Trump’s anti-trans orders 
 by Oliver Willis 
 Staff 
 Friday, October 23, 2026 at 4:00 PM PDT 
 Recommend Story 
 Save 
 39 Comments 
 Add Daily Kos to Google 
 A person wears a trans equality flag in their hair while attending a rally on the National Mall in 2025. AP 
 The Trump administration is facing an unexpected obstacle in its crusade to segregate the military and kick out transgender troops who have signed up to defend their country—and that obstacle is the armed services themselves.
 The New York Times reports that review boards set up to execute President Donald Trump’s orders to consider the cases of transgender troops before ultimately removing them are, in at least two branches of the armed services, not giving the administration the rubber stamp it anticipated.
 In 12 cases that have come before the Navy and the Marines, boards have voted to retain troops nine times. The Trump purge has been more successful in the Air Force and Army, where troops are more likely to be removed.
 Former Air Force lawyer Rachel VanLandingham explained the quiet rebellion to the Times, “We are seeing them nullify a process they see as unjust.”
 Marine Staff Sgt. Damien Contreras, who was singled out by the administration for removal but whose review board determined he “remains qualified,” explained the mindset of his fellow servicemembers to the outlet.
 “They see I’ve always done my job, I’ve deployed, I’ve mentored other Marines, followed the rules. They say, ‘Hey, this is a good Marine, why wouldn’t we retain him?’” he said.
 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, shown in July. AP 
 Contreras’ statement underlines the destructive stance of the administration. If the American military wants to continue to be the most powerful fighting force in the world—fulfilling Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s endless ranting about retaining “war fighters”—shouldn’t able and willing transgender servicemembers be a key part of the equation?
 The decision by these review boards to defy Hegseth and Trump is in line with earlier reporting that for all the public bravado expressed by the two Republicans, rank-and-file members of the military do not have respect for the men and their dictates.
 To be sure, the boards’ findings can be overruled by political appointees, but the sheer act of quiet defiance undermines years of conservative rhetoric purporting that the movement has the unified support of the armed services.
 While attempting to root out transgender service members, Hegseth has also acted to block promotions that were slated to occur for Black and female officers. The former Fox News host who once bragged that he never washes his hands has even put in rules about beard length and shaving that would disproportionately single out Black soldiers for removal.
 In a time of peace, the right wing’s push to turn the military into something resembling a conservative safe space consisting of only straight white men (with appropriate testosterone levels ) might still be controversial, but Hegseth’s ideas are being implemented while America is stuck in yet another war in the Middle East, with no end in sight.
 If battlefield triumph is the end goal—and that’s the entire point of having such a well-financed military—you wouldn’t undermine the fighting force by drumming out the best and the brightest.
 But that is precisely what Trump and Hegseth are trying to do, and some of the troops seem to have had enough.
